reason: E1 shows that low-melting-point elements (Cu) can preferentially dissolve and diffuse during alloy processing, supporting the mobility and segregation premise, but it describes mechanical alloying at room temperature, not heating of a pre-formed solid solution. E2 and E3 mention segregation in other contexts but do not directly address Cu segregation during heating of solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles. The key premise that Cu enrichment locally lowers the melting point and initiates premelting lacks direct cited evidence.
premises: Copper has a significantly lower melting point than Fe, Ni, Cr, Co
Lower-melting-point elements exhibit higher atomic mobility at elevated temperatures
Higher mobility drives nanoscale segregation of Cu to surfaces/grain boundaries during heating
Local Cu enrichment reduces the local melting point, initiating premelting
Elemental segregation can occur in high-entropy alloys during thermal processing
